points.description: States that the address-of operator (&) returns the memory address (location in memory) of its operand. 'Address' must be stated as a memory address; vague answers like 'a location' or 'the value' earn nothing.
points.partial_credit: Half (1.5) if it says it returns an address but not precisely that it is a memory address, or does not link it to the operand.

points.description: Makes clear the address returned is that of its operand (the variable/object the operator is applied to), e.g. &x gives the address of x, not x's value.
Correctly distinguishes it from the value: the result is the address where the operand is stored (a pointer value), not the contents/value of the operand (that is the dereference * operator).

rubric.notes: Full marks need a precise statement that & returns the memory address of its operand, with the address clearly distinguished from the operand's value. Part marks only if clearly more than half of a point is stated precisely, such as saying 'address' without 'memory' or the operand. Any wrong statement (e.g. says it returns the value) earns nothing for that point; generic or implied wording earns nothing.
